actions.text: Acting alone, it pulls the arm in and forward across the front of the chest and rotates it inward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, II. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Anterior and Lateral Thoracic Walls, Actions (p. 439); Pectoralis major
cite.quote: it adducts and draws forward the arm, bringing it across the front of the chest, and at the same time rotates it inward

actions.text: With the latissimus dorsi and teres major, it brings a raised arm back down to the side of the chest.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, II. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Anterior and Lateral Thoracic Walls, Actions (p. 439); Pectoralis major, when the arm has been raised
cite.quote: conjointly with the Latissimus dorsi and Teres major, depress it to the side of the chest

actions.text: Raises the arm out from the side until it is at a right angle to the trunk.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, III. The Muscles and Fasciae of the Shoulder, Deltoideus, Actions (p. 440)
cite.quote: The Deltoideus raises the arm from the side, so as to bring it at right angles with the trunk.

actions.text: Its front fibers, helped by the pectoralis major, draw the arm forward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, III. The Muscles and Fasciae of the Shoulder, Deltoideus, Actions (p. 440)
cite.quote: Its anterior fibers, assisted by the Pectoralis major, draw the arm forward

actions.text: Its rear fibers, helped by the teres major and latissimus dorsi, draw the arm backward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, III. The Muscles and Fasciae of the Shoulder, Deltoideus, Actions (p. 440)
cite.quote: its posterior fibers, aided by the Teres major and Latissimus dorsi, draw it backward

actions.text: Pulls the upper arm down and back and rotates it inward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, I. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Vertebral Column, Actions (p. 435); Latissimus dorsi
cite.quote: When the Latissimus dorsi acts upon the humerus, it depresses and draws it backward, and at the same time rotates it inward.

actions.text: Gray 1918 calls it the main muscle used for a downward blow, as in chopping down a tree.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, I. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Vertebral Column, Actions (p. 435); Latissimus dorsi
cite.quote: It is the muscle which is principally employed in giving a downward blow, as in felling a tree

actions.text: With both arms fixed, the two latissimus muscles help hang the body from the arms and pull the trunk forward (Gray's example is climbing).

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, I. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Vertebral Column, Actions (p. 435); Latissimus dorsi, with the arms fixed
cite.quote: if both arms be fixed, the two muscles may assist the abdominal muscles and Pectorales in suspending and drawing the trunk forward

actions.text: The whole trapezius pulls the shoulder blade back and braces the shoulder back.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, I. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Vertebral Column, Actions (p. 435); Trapezius
cite.quote: When the whole Trapezius is in action it retracts the scapula and braces back the shoulder

actions.text: With the head fixed, its upper part raises the point of the shoulder, as when supporting weights.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, I. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Vertebral Column, Actions (p. 435); Trapezius, upper part
cite.quote: if the head be fixed, the upper part of the muscle will elevate the point of the shoulder, as in supporting weights

actions.text: Its middle and lower fibers rotate the shoulder blade so that the top of the shoulder (acromion) rises.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, I. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Vertebral Column, Actions (p. 435); Trapezius, middle and lower fibers
cite.quote: The middle and lower fibers of the muscle rotate the scapula, causing elevation of the acromion.

actions.text: Pulls the shoulder blade forward and raises its inner (spine-side) border.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, II. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Anterior and Lateral Thoracic Walls, Actions (p. 439); Serratus anterior
cite.quote: The Serratus anterior, as a whole, carries the scapula forward, and at the same time raises the vertebral border of the bone.

actions.text: It is involved in pushing.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, II. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Anterior and Lateral Thoracic Walls, Actions (p. 439); Serratus anterior
cite.quote: It is therefore concerned in the action of pushing.

actions.text: Together with the trapezius, it rotates the shoulder blade to raise the arm to nearly vertical.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, II. The Muscles Connecting the Upper Extremity to the Anterior and Lateral Thoracic Walls, Actions (p. 439); Serratus anterior, after the deltoid has raised the arm to a right angle
cite.quote: the Serratus anterior and the Trapezius, by rotating the scapula, raise the arm into an almost vertical position

actions.text: Bends the elbow and, to a lesser extent, flexes the shoulder; it is also a powerful supinator (turns the palm up).

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, IV. The Muscles and Fasciae of the Arm, Actions (p. 444); Biceps brachii
cite.quote: The Biceps brachii is a flexor of the elbow and, to a less extent, of the shoulder; it is also a powerful supinator

actions.text: With the forearm fixed, the biceps and brachialis pull the upper arm toward the forearm, as in climbing.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, IV. The Muscles and Fasciae of the Arm, Actions (p. 444); Biceps brachii and Brachialis, with the forearm fixed
cite.quote: When the forearm is fixed, the Biceps brachii and Brachialis flex the arm upon the forearm, as in efforts of climbing.

actions.text: The main muscle that straightens the elbow; it directly opposes the biceps and brachialis.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, IV. The Muscles and Fasciae of the Arm, Triceps brachii, Actions (p. 445)
cite.quote: The Triceps brachii is the great extensor muscle of the forearm, and is the direct antagonist of the Biceps brachii and Brachialis.

actions.text: With the arm extended, its long head can help the teres major and latissimus dorsi draw the upper arm backward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, IV. The Muscles and Fasciae of the Arm, Triceps brachii, Actions (p. 445); long head
cite.quote: When the arm is extended, the long head of the muscle may assist the Teres major and Latissimus dorsi in drawing the humerus backward

actions.text: Working from below, the rectus abdominis pulls the rib cage down and so bends the spine forward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, The Antero-lateral Muscles of the Abdomen, Actions (p. 418); the Recti
cite.quote: The Recti, acting from below, depress the thorax, and consequently flex the vertebral column

actions.text: Working from above, it tilts the pelvis up toward the spine (flexes the pelvis on the vertebral column).

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, The Antero-lateral Muscles of the Abdomen, Actions (p. 418); the Recti
cite.quote: when acting from above, they flex the pelvis upon the vertebral column.

actions.text: With the pelvis fixed, the abdominal muscles of both sides (as a group) bend the trunk straight forward. Group statement.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, The Antero-lateral Muscles of the Abdomen, Actions (p. 417); group statement, for the antero-lateral abdominal muscles together
cite.quote: If the pelvis alone be fixed, the thorax is bent directly forward, when the muscles of both sides act

actions.text: Extends the hip, bringing a bent thigh back into line with the body.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 3. The Muscles of the Gluteal Region, Actions (p. 478); Glutaeus maximus, taking its fixed point from the pelvis
cite.quote: it extends the femur and brings the bent thigh into a line with the body

actions.text: Its most powerful action is bringing the body back upright after bending over, by pulling the pelvis back.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 3. The Muscles of the Gluteal Region, Actions (p. 478); Glutaeus maximus
cite.quote: Its most powerful action is to cause the body to regain the erect position after stooping, by drawing the pelvis backward

actions.text: Its lower part also adducts and rotates the thigh outward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 3. The Muscles of the Gluteal Region, Actions (p. 478); Glutaeus maximus, lower part
cite.quote: The lower part of the muscle also acts as an adductor and external rotator

actions.text: Straightens the knee.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 1. The Anterior Femoral Muscles, Actions (p. 471); Quadriceps femoris
cite.quote: The Quadriceps femoris extends the leg upon the thigh.

actions.text: The rectus femoris part also helps flex the hip (or, with the thigh fixed, tilts the pelvis forward).

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 1. The Anterior Femoral Muscles, Actions (p. 471); Rectus femoris (the sentence's subject is the Rectus femoris)
cite.quote: It also assists in flexing the thigh on the pelvis, or if the thigh be fixed it will flex the pelvis.

actions.text: The vastus medialis pulls the kneecap inward as well as upward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 1. The Anterior Femoral Muscles, Actions (p. 471); Vastus medialis
cite.quote: The Vastus medialis draws the patella medialward as well as upward.

actions.text: The hamstrings (as a group) bend the knee. Group statement, not specific to this muscle.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 4. The Posterior Femoral Muscles (Hamstring Muscles), Actions (p. 480); group statement, for all three hamstrings together
cite.quote: The hamstring muscles flex the leg upon the thigh.

actions.text: With the knee half bent, the biceps femoris rotates the lower leg slightly outward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 4. The Posterior Femoral Muscles (Hamstring Muscles), Actions (p. 480); Biceps femoris
cite.quote: When the knee is semiflexed, the Biceps femoris in consequence of its oblique direction rotates the leg slightly outward

actions.text: Working from below, the hamstrings (as a group) support the pelvis on the thigh bone and pull the trunk straight back, as when rising from a stooped position. Group statement.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 4. The Posterior Femoral Muscles (Hamstring Muscles), Actions (p. 480); group statement, for all three hamstrings together
cite.quote: these muscles serve to support the pelvis upon the head of the femur, and to draw the trunk directly backward

actions.text: The hamstrings (as a group) bend the knee. Group statement, not specific to this muscle.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 4. The Posterior Femoral Muscles (Hamstring Muscles), Actions (p. 480); group statement, for all three hamstrings together
cite.quote: The hamstring muscles flex the leg upon the thigh.

actions.text: With the knee half bent, the semitendinosus, and to a slight extent the semimembranosus, rotate the lower leg inward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 4. The Posterior Femoral Muscles (Hamstring Muscles), Actions (p. 480); sentence names semitendinosus and semimembranosus
cite.quote: the Semitendinosus, and to a slight extent the Semimembranosus, rotate the leg inward

actions.text: Working from below, the hamstrings (as a group) support the pelvis on the thigh bone and pull the trunk straight back, as when rising from a stooped position. Group statement.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 4. The Posterior Femoral Muscles (Hamstring Muscles), Actions (p. 480); group statement, for all three hamstrings together
cite.quote: these muscles serve to support the pelvis upon the head of the femur, and to draw the trunk directly backward

actions.text: The hamstrings (as a group) bend the knee. Group statement, not specific to this muscle.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 4. The Posterior Femoral Muscles (Hamstring Muscles), Actions (p. 480); group statement, for all three hamstrings together
cite.quote: The hamstring muscles flex the leg upon the thigh.

actions.text: With the knee half bent, the semitendinosus, and to a slight extent the semimembranosus, rotate the lower leg inward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 4. The Posterior Femoral Muscles (Hamstring Muscles), Actions (p. 480); sentence names semitendinosus and semimembranosus
cite.quote: the Semitendinosus, and to a slight extent the Semimembranosus, rotate the leg inward

actions.text: Working from below, the hamstrings (as a group) support the pelvis on the thigh bone and pull the trunk straight back, as when rising from a stooped position. Group statement.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 4. The Posterior Femoral Muscles (Hamstring Muscles), Actions (p. 480); group statement, for all three hamstrings together
cite.quote: these muscles serve to support the pelvis upon the head of the femur, and to draw the trunk directly backward

actions.text: The calf muscles (as a group) are the main muscles that point the foot down at the ankle (plantar flexion; Gray 1918 calls this 'extension' of the foot).

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 2. The Posterior Crural Muscles, Superficial Group, Actions (p. 483); group statement, for the calf muscles together
cite.quote: The muscles of the calf are the chief extensors of the foot at the ankle-joint.

actions.text: In walking, the calf muscles (as a group) lift the heel off the ground.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 2. The Posterior Crural Muscles, Superficial Group, Actions (p. 483); group statement, for the calf muscles together
cite.quote: In walking, these muscles raise the heel from the ground

actions.text: Working from below, the gastrocnemius helps bend the knee (flexes the thigh bone on the shin bone).

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 2. The Posterior Crural Muscles, Superficial Group, Actions (p. 483); Gastrocnemius
cite.quote: The Gastrocnemius, acting from below, serves to flex the femur upon the tibia

actions.text: The calf muscles (as a group) are the main muscles that point the foot down at the ankle (plantar flexion; Gray 1918 calls this 'extension' of the foot).

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 2. The Posterior Crural Muscles, Superficial Group, Actions (p. 483); group statement, for the calf muscles together
cite.quote: The muscles of the calf are the chief extensors of the foot at the ankle-joint.

actions.text: In walking, the calf muscles (as a group) lift the heel off the ground.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 2. The Posterior Crural Muscles, Superficial Group, Actions (p. 483); group statement, for the calf muscles together
cite.quote: In walking, these muscles raise the heel from the ground

actions.text: In standing, the soleus steadies the lower leg over the foot and keeps the body from falling forward.

cite.locator: Gray 1918, Myology, 2. The Posterior Crural Muscles, Superficial Group, Actions (p. 483); Soleus
cite.quote: In standing, the Soleus, taking its fixed point from below, steadies the leg upon the foot and prevents the body from falling forward.
